title: ci: fail the Node pin guard when the pinned runtime is out of support (#3825)
body:
Follow-up to #3830. Closes the blind spot that PR left behind.

## Consistency was only half the invariant

`check-node-version` (added in #3830) proves all 18 workflows agree on a Node version. **It would have said `OK` just as cheerfully when all 18 agreed on Node 20, three months after that line went EOL** — which is exactly the state #3825 found the repo in.

So the guard as shipped defends against *drift* but not against *expiry*. If `.nvmrc` sits at 22 until 2027-04-30 and beyond, it stays green the whole way. The only thing that caught the last expiry was someone tripping over it by accident (#3812).

## What the guard now also checks

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| Pin is past EOL | **error** — an unpatched runtime is guarding every merge |
| Pin is within 180 days of EOL | **`::warning::`** on the PR |
| Pin is a major the guard has no dates for | **error** |

**Warn-then-fail, not fail-early.** A hard failure months ahead of EOL would block unrelated PRs on a random day; 180 days of warnings visible on every PR make the bump scheduled work instead. The hard stop lands only when support actually ends — which is the thing we agreed must not happen.

**Unknown major is an error, not a pass.** Adopting Node 26 forces you to record its dates rather than silently validating on a runtime this guard knows nothing about. Same fail-closed shape as the `${{ }}` case in #3830.

Dates come from `nodejs/Release` `schedule.json`, hardcoded on purpose: a required gate must not depend on the network, and they move once a year.

## Verified — all four paths

```
GREEN     check-node-version: OK (18 setup-node step(s) across 16 workflow(s), all on Node 22).
            Node 22 is in maintenance; supported until 2027-04-30 (276 days).

EOL       .nvmrc pins Node 20, which reached end-of-life on 2026-04-30 (89 days ago).
          Supported today: 22 (until 2027-04-30), 24 (until 2028-04-30), 26 (until 2029-04-30).

UNKNOWN   .nvmrc pins Node "99", which this guard has no support dates for.
          Add it to NODE_LIFECYCLE … Known: 18, 20, 22, 24, 26.

WARNING   ::warning file=.nvmrc::Node 22 reaches end-of-life on 2027-04-30 (276 days)…
```

(The warning path was exercised by temporarily widening the 180-day threshold to 300, then restoring it.)

## Worth knowing, but deliberately not acted on here

The new success line surfaces this:

> `Node 22 is in maintenance; supported until 2027-04-30 (276 days).`

**Node 22 entered maintenance on 2025-10-21, and Node 24 has been Active LTS since 2025-10-28.** So the runtime we just standardised on is already the older of the two supported LTS lines. #3825 raised this ("Consider 24 instead if a longer window matters") and chose 22 as the lower-risk move, which was right for that PR — 6 workflows already ran it.

Moving to 24 is now a one-line `.nvmrc` edit plus whatever this guard lists. That is a separate decision; **nothing in this PR forces or schedules it.**
